name: Root-Avoiding Decompositions and Convex Root Tests
statement: A pointed cover-recursively peripheral partial cube $(A,a)$ has a root-avoiding peripheral decomposition exactly when every nontrivial convex subgraph containing $a$ has a peripheral semicube omitting $a$. This pointed class is closed under coordinate contractions and restrictions to semicubes containing the root. Its pointed-minor-minimal nonmembers are exactly the root-critical pairs: root-locked pairs whose root-side restriction and contraction in every coordinate have root-avoiding decompositions.
proof: Root-preserving minors commute past the first root-avoiding peripheral step; induction preserves the rooted contraction base and uses ordinary pc-minor closure for the duplicated site. Hence every convex subgraph containing the root inherits an avoiding periphery. Conversely, choose such a periphery in the original graph. Its opposite side is the rooted contraction base and inherits the convex test, while the duplicated site is a convex member of the unpointed class; induction reconstructs a root-avoiding decomposition. Pointed minimality is then equivalent to root-locking plus repair of every immediate rooted minor.
